name: network
title: Network
description: This machine's addresses: every interface's IPs (the Wi-Fi one with its SSID), the public IP with its country and ISP, the default gateway, the DNS servers, the Tailscale IP, the hostname. Enter copies the value.
author: pal

settings.label: Public IP endpoint
settings.description: Fetched with a 3 s timeout and kept 10 minutes; JSON with `ip` (and `city`, `country`, `org` when it has them) or a bare address. Empty: no public IP row.

settings.label: SSID labels
settings.description: Optional friendly names as `SSID = label`, for example `Cafe Wifi = Cafe`. The Network bar uses the label; the palette still shows the real SSID.

settings.label: Known networks
settings.description: What a network is, as `SSID = kind` or `gateway = kind`; the gateway form also covers a cable into the same router and a Wi-Fi name macOS declines to reveal. `hide` drops the bar item entirely — the network you are on almost all the time can tell you nothing, so its absence is the point. `hotspot` marks one that costs data, `public` one to distrust. For example `eldiven = hide`, `192.168.1.1 = hide`, `marvin = hotspot`.

settings.label: Network icons
settings.description: A network's own glyph on the bar and its palette rows, as `SSID = glyph` or `gateway = glyph` (the gateway form covers a cable and a redacted name, as in Known networks). The glyph is one emoji or a Nerd Font glyph pasted in (the Icons palette copies one). It replaces the signal, hotspot, open or wired mark; the tooltip and the popover still say those. For example `eldiven = 󰋜`, `192.168.1.1 = 🏠`, `marvin = 📱`.

settings.label: Icon only
settings.text: Drop the name from the bar item; the glyph still says wired, hotspot, open or how strong the signal is, and hovering gives the name.

store.tagline: Every IP this machine has right now, Enter copies it
features: This machine: each interface's IPv4 and global IPv6 (`en0 · Wi-Fi`, `eth0`), the Tailscale IPv4 and IPv6, the hostname and the Bonjour `.local` name
Internet: the public IP with the city, country and organisation the endpoint gives, fetched once and kept ten minutes
Network: the default gateway with its interface, the DNS servers in resolver order
The value is the row's name, so it reads at a glance; `enter` copies it, `cmd+enter` opens the Network settings
Opens with the detail pane: interface, kind, SSID, security, signal, MAC and status for an address; city, region and organisation for the public IP
Live: listed again when the panel shows and the last listing is over a minute old; `cmd+r` fetches the public IP again

actions.title: Open Network settings
actions.description: System Settings on macOS; gnome-control-center, systemsettings or nm-connection-editor on Linux.

network.description: Live rows, listed again when the panel shows and the last listing is over a minute old; ⌘R lists now and fetches the public IP again.

status.title: Network status
status.description: The active network, as its name or — with Icon only — as a glyph alone: signal strength on Wi-Fi, its own mark for a hotspot or an open network, wired, or offline, or the glyph Network icons gives that network (home, office, cafe, phone). A network set to `hide` in Known networks draws nothing. Click opens Network Settings; the popover names the connection and its kind, then the interface, the address, the gateway, the signal and security, and the DNS servers.
